title: Aurum Alpha feature flag declaration
description: standards/038-feature-flags.md FF2: one flag's declaration, committed beside the code that evaluates it and built into the image. The repository's declaration file is a list of these; a name appears once. The provider holds values; this holds existence and lifetime. Conditional rules the prose states and a reviewer would otherwise remember: release and experiment flags carry expires and removal and never review_by (FF3); operational and entitlement flags carry review_by and never expires (FF3); an experiment carries two or more variants (FF10); a boolean flag's default is false (FF4). The 180-day ceiling on expires after created, and the 365-day ceiling on review_by ahead of the reading date, (FF3) are date computations the expiry corpus part decides, not this schema. schemaVersion 1 — evolves additively per PC6.

flagName.description: FF2: <area>.<flag>, lowercase snake_case segments, exactly two. The key passed to the evaluation API and the feature_flag.key on the span. Has the shape of a permission string and is never one (FF5): the two sets are disjoint.

scalar.description: A value a string or number flag may take.

type.description: FF1: which typed evaluation call resolves it. A provider value of another type is TYPE_MISMATCH and returns the default (FF4).

default.description: FF4: what every evaluation returns when the provider does not answer — not ready, unreachable, flag unknown, type mismatch, targeting key missing. For a boolean flag this is false; for a string or number flag it is the variant the code shipped with. The call site's default is this value.

kind.description: FF3: which lifetime the flag has. release and experiment expire; operational and entitlement are reviewed.

scope.description: FF6: which public id is the targeting key — the tenant's for tenant, the user's for user, none for global. A scoped flag evaluated without its id returns the default with TARGETING_KEY_MISSING.

description.description: FF2: what true, or each variant, turns on. Written for the reviewer who finds the flag overdue.

owner.description: FF2: the team or role handle asked when the sweep finds the flag overdue (FF11). A handle, never a person's name or address: the file is in the repository.

created.description: FF3: the start of the lifetime. RFC 3339 full-date per 020 IP4.

expires.description: FF3: the last day a release or experiment flag is in date; the day after, the sweep raises a finding. At most 180 days after created (decided by the expiry corpus part). Forbidden on operational and entitlement flags.

review_by.description: FF3: the last day an operational or entitlement flag is in date without review; the day after, the sweep raises a finding. At most 365 days ahead of the day the declaration is read — measured forward from the reading and not from created, because what is bounded here is neglect rather than life (decided by the expiry corpus part, not this schema). Forbidden on release and experiment flags.

removal.description: FF3, FF11: the condition under which the flag and its call sites are deleted, written at creation. Required on release and experiment flags; for an experiment it is where the decision is recorded (FF10).

variants.description: FF10: the admitted values of a string or number flag. An experiment declares two or more. Not admitted on boolean or object flags, whose values are their type.

served_to_client.description: FF7: whether the flag's evaluated value is included in the set the browser receives. Off by default; a flag the browser does not render from is not sent to it.
